title: Every Atlas Interpretation must set a clear precedent, converting one-off rulings into permanent constraints
content:
A.1.1.2 imposes three cumulative requirements on any Atlas Interpretation: it must be "fully congruent with the Spirit of the Atlas and established precedent," and "each Atlas Interpretation must set a clear precedent to avoid future ambiguities that could impede effective governance." A.1.1.2.1 adds that "all Atlas Interpretations must be documented."

The combination builds a ratchet. Congruence with prior precedent means an interpreter cannot decide the same question differently next time; the obligation to *set* clear precedent means each ruling narrows the space available to future interpreters. Discretion is therefore spent, not renewed — every use of it permanently reduces the amount remaining.

A.1.1.3.1 makes this concrete in an unglamorous way: interpretations are recorded as Active Data with the Core Facilitator as Responsible Party, updated by 'Direct Edit'. A.1.1.3.1.0.6.1 shows the list currently holds a single entry, about SKY-denominated payments being made in MKR before SKY launches.

The design bet is that a precedent-bound interpreter with broad discretion is safer than a narrowly-bounded one, because bounded discretion invites letter-of-the-rule gaming while precedent-bound discretion accumulates a body of reasoning that is auditable. The cost is that a bad early precedent is expensive to unwind.
description: Interpretations must be congruent with the Spirit AND with prior precedent, so discretion is spent rather than renewed: each ruling narrows the space left to future interpreters.
